mainEntity.name: Does the file pass through your servers?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A small signaling server only helps two devices discover each other and negotiate a direct WebRTC connection; the actual file bytes travel peer-to-peer, never through our infrastructure.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an account to use this?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — pairing is done per-session with a QR code or link; there's nothing to sign up for and nothing is stored afterward.

mainEntity.name: Can I send to more than one device at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Each session pairs two devices. For multiple recipients, open a new session per pair.

mainEntity.name: Is my image uploaded to a server to upscale it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — the upscaling model runs locally via onnxruntime-web. Nothing is sent over the network during processing.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between 2× and 4×?

acceptedAnswer.text: 4× produces four times the linear resolution (16× the pixel count) of the source and takes proportionally longer to compute.

mainEntity.name: Does upscaling work on illustrations and screenshots, not just photos?

acceptedAnswer.text: It's tuned for photographic detail; flat illustrations and UI screenshots can look over-sharpened. For those, a simple resize may look cleaner.

mainEntity.name: Will compressing make my text blurry or unselectable?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compression re-renders each page as an image at your chosen quality, so text stays sharp at Light and Balanced but is no longer selectable or searchable afterward — the same trade-off as scanning a printed page. Keep an uncompressed copy if you need selectable text.

mainEntity.name: How much smaller will my file get?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on content and the level you pick. Image-heavy and scanned PDFs often shrink 50–80% at Balanced or Aggressive; already-compact text PDFs shrink less.

mainEntity.name: Is there a page limit?

acceptedAnswer.text: No fixed limit — it's set by your browser's available memory, not a server-side cap.

mainEntity.name: Is this 'true' redaction, or just a black box on top?

acceptedAnswer.text: True redaction. Export rasterizes each redacted page into a flat image, so there's no hidden text layer left to copy or search out.

mainEntity.name: Will the rest of the PDF's pages be affected?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — only pages you draw a redaction on are flattened; untouched pages keep their original text and quality.

mainEntity.name: Can I undo a redaction before exporting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, redactions are editable up until you click Flatten & Export; after export, the change is permanent by design.

mainEntity.name: Is my recording uploaded anywhere while I record?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. MediaRecorder writes the video to memory in your browser, and the Trust Meter confirms zero bytes are sent over the network for the entire session.

mainEntity.name: What format does the download come in?

acceptedAnswer.text: WebM by default, since that's what MediaRecorder produces natively in most browsers. Some browsers can export MP4 directly.

mainEntity.name: Can I record just a browser tab and not my whole desktop?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — when you click Start, the browser's own picker lets you choose a tab, a window, or the entire screen.

mainEntity.name: Is my audio or video uploaded to transcribe it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Transcription runs Whisper entirely in your browser via transformers.js — WebGPU when available, WASM otherwise. Nothing is sent over the network during processing.

mainEntity.name: Why does it need to download a model first?

acceptedAnswer.text: The speech-recognition model itself is 100–300MB depending on the quality tier you pick. It's downloaded once and cached, so later visits and later files skip that step.

mainEntity.name: Which languages are supported?

acceptedAnswer.text: Whisper supports dozens of languages; recognition quality varies by language and is generally strongest for widely-spoken ones with more training data.

mainEntity.name: Is my video uploaded to a server to compress it?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — this runs ffmpeg compiled to WebAssembly, executing entirely inside your browser tab. The Trust Meter confirms nothing is sent over the network during processing.

mainEntity.name: How long does compression take?

acceptedAnswer.text: Roughly proportional to video length and your device's CPU — expect it to take a noticeable fraction of the video's own runtime, longer on older hardware.

mainEntity.name: Why does the tool need to download something first?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ffmpeg engine itself is a ~30MB WebAssembly module. It's fetched once and cached by your browser, so repeat visits skip the download.
